evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The three tastings in server/catalog.ts:4-8 match the brief. The start page shows title, date and time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (TastingCard.tsx:28-47, start.jpg). Each card has a 'Book <title>' link (TastingCard.tsx:53-55). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1 to 8) and a 'Book' button (BookingPage.tsx:112-142). Seat limits are enforced on the server (store.ts:107-113), and field errors appear under the field they concern (form.jpg shows 'Enter a valid email address' under Email). The confirmation shows the 'Booking confirmed' heading, the tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:75-102, confirmation.jpg shows EUR 64 for 2 x 32). /staff has a Password field and a 'Sign in' button, and reads STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:7, StaffPage.tsx:201-211). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button (StaffPage.tsx:123-160, staff.jpg). Cancelling frees seats because seats are derived from the bookings (store.ts:92-100). The interface uses React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. npm start honours PORT with default 3000 (index.ts:5). Bookings start empty and are kept in a local JSON file.
evidence.correctness: Every change to the bookings runs through a promise queue (store.ts:161-166), so two concurrent bookings cannot both take the last seats. store.test.ts:88-99 covers this race. A failed save rolls back both bookings and cancellations (store.ts:121-127, 138-143). seatsLeft is clamped at 0 (store.ts:99). The fully-booked and not-enough-seats cases return distinct messages, with singular wording for one seat (app.ts:53-59). Guests input is strict: 2.5, true, [2] and '' are rejected (schemas.ts:25-28, schemas.test.ts:49). Once a booking is cancelled, its confirmation link returns 404. A corrupt data file stops startup and is left unchanged (store.ts:215-235). The Book button is disabled while the request is in flight. After a 409 the page refreshes the seat count (BookingPage.tsx:62). The only edge case I found is in the staff flow: Cancel acts immediately, with no confirmation step (StaffPage.tsx:151).
evidence.security: Passwords are compared as SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual (staffAuth.ts:84-88). The session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and its key is random per process (staffAuth.ts:11-19). Sessions are also tracked on the server with an 8-hour expiry, so a copied cookie stops working after sign-out (staffAuth.ts:24-58, staff.test.ts:148-165). helmet adds a CSP, the JSON body is capped at 10kb, and staff routes check the session (app.ts:28-31, 102). Login is rate-limited to 10 failures per 15 minutes. React escapes all output, and the code uses no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No secrets are in code. The public confirmation endpoint leaves out name and email (api.test.ts:112-123). Weaknesses: 'trust proxy' is never set, yet the README (line 34) recommends running behind a TLS proxy. Behind that proxy every client shares one IP for the rate limiter, so 10 wrong guesses by anyone lock staff out for 15 minutes. The cookie is also not Secure (this is documented).
evidence.code_quality: Responsibilities are cleanly split: catalog, store, auth, app and entry point on the server, with zod schemas and types shared between client and server (shared/). The store uses discriminated result types (store.ts:24-28). Names are clear, error handling is consistent (ApiErrorBody with field errors or a message, and a central error handler at app.ts:162-170), and TypeScript runs in strict mode. Components are small (Field, Notice, TastingCard) and there is no needless abstraction. Comments explain why, not what.
evidence.tests: The tests cover all layers. Schema tests check boundaries: 0, 9, 2.5, '' and 100/101-character names. Store tests cover the seat limit, exact fill, the concurrent race, rollback on a failed save, persistence across restart and the file mode. API tests cover status codes, field errors and the shell fallback. Staff tests cover login, rate limiting, revocation, 8-hour expiry and cancel freeing seats. Component tests cover each page with RTL, including aria-describedby links. Playwright e2e (test/e2e/booking.spec.ts) runs the whole flow, including cancelling to free seats, plus a 360px phone check for overflow and 44px tap targets.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: cream paper, wine red, serif headings and a wine-coloured rule under the header (start.jpg). The cards are clean. The error state is a red border with the message underneath (form.jpg). The success state is a green check with a clear summary list and a prominent reference (confirmation.jpg). The code adds a fully-booked badge and replaces the form with a notice (TastingCard.tsx:21-25, BookingPage.tsx:99-103). The layout is responsive and tested at 360px. Gaps: the staff view shows no seat totals per tasting (staff.jpg). Cancel has no confirmation or undo. The footer still says 'Staff sign-in' while staff are signed in (staff.jpg). The page has no imagery at all, only text cards.
evidence.accessibility: Every field has a label linked with htmlFor (Field.tsx:14-23). Errors set aria-invalid and are linked through aria-describedby. Form-level notices use role=alert (Notice.tsx:15). Articles and staff sections are labelled by their headings. The app uses dl/dt/dd and a time element with dateTime, sets lang=en and updates the document title per page. Focus-visible outlines are styled, and tap targets are at least 44px. The palette comment claims AA contrast, and the colours I checked look sufficient. Gaps: several 'Cancel' buttons have identical accessible names, with nothing naming the guest or reference (StaffPage.tsx:151). Field-level errors are not in a live region; they rely on react-hook-form focusing the first invalid field.
evidence.simplicity: The dependency set is reasonable for the brief: Express, helmet, rate-limit, cookie-session, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. There is no database. The code is compact. Some parts are more than a small winery needs: an fsync'd atomic write with a directory sync (store.ts:185-213), cookie-session layered on a server-side session map, and the injectable write and clock hooks. All are justified, but they add weight.
evidence.maintainability: The README is good: run steps, env vars (PORT, STAFF_PASSWORD, DATA_FILE), operating notes, dev workflow, test commands and a layout section. A package-lock exists, engines requires node >=22.12, and there are typecheck and test scripts. Missing: there is no CI pipeline. There is no .nvmrc or .node-version. The README (line 62) points to openspec/changes/add-tasting-bookings, but the delivered openspec/ contains only specs/.gitkeep, so the referenced spec and decision history are absent. There are no ADRs, no changelog or release process beyond version 1.0.0, and no staff guide beyond the README. Dependencies use caret ranges, pinned only through the lockfile.

strengths: Robust booking logic: seats are derived from the bookings, changes run through a serialized queue so concurrent bookings cannot overbook, and a failed save is rolled back (server/store.ts:59-181).
Strong staff security: timing-safe digest comparison, HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, server-side revocable sessions with 8h expiry, rate-limited login, helmet CSP.
Thorough tests at every layer (schema, store, API, components, Playwright e2e including 360px mobile checks), all tied directly to the brief's requirements.
issues: No CI pipeline, no .nvmrc, and the README references spec and decision history (openspec/changes/add-tasting-bookings) that is not in the repository; there are no ADRs and no release process.
Without 'trust proxy', the recommended TLS-proxy deployment makes all clients share one rate-limit bucket, so 10 wrong guesses by anyone lock staff out for 15 minutes.
Staff UX gaps: Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation, the Cancel buttons have indistinguishable accessible names, and staff see no booked or remaining seat totals per tasting.
review.verdict: This is a polished, correct and well-tested booking app that meets every requirement in the brief, with careful concurrency handling and solid staff authentication. It is shippable after small fixes: add CI and the missing spec docs, set trust proxy for the deployment, and add a confirmation step to staff cancel.
